keyboard.settings_section: Command palette entry that opens one Settings section. {section} = settings section name, e.g. "Privacy". Keep short, about 25 characters.
keyboard.open_settings: Command palette action that opens the Settings page. Keep short, about 15 characters.
keyboard.check_updates: Command palette action that checks for an app update. Keep short, about 20 characters.
keyboard.support: Command palette action that opens the support page. Contains "Deadlock+", which stays untranslated. Keep short, about 20 characters.
keyboard.open_palette: Command palette entry in the keyboard shortcuts group. Names the shortcut that opens this search box. Keep short, about 15 characters.
keyboard.jump: Command palette entry in the keyboard shortcuts group. Names the shortcut that jumps to a page by number. Keep short, about 15 characters.
keyboard.palette_title: Screen reader only title of the quick search dialog (command palette). Not visible on screen.
keyboard.palette_description: Screen reader only description of the quick search dialog (command palette). Not visible on screen.
keyboard.palette_placeholder: Placeholder text in the quick search input at the top of the command palette.
keyboard.palette_input_label: Screen reader label for the quick search input in the command palette.
keyboard.no_match: Empty state in the quick search list when no command matches what the user typed.

groups.pages: Group heading in the quick search list for page entries. Keep short, about 8 characters.
groups.settings: Group heading in the quick search list for settings entries. Keep short, about 10 characters.
groups.actions: Group heading in the quick search list for action entries. Keep short, about 10 characters.
groups.shortcuts: Group heading in the quick search list for entries that describe keyboard shortcuts. Keep short, about 20 characters.

keywords.page: Hidden search keywords for page entries in quick search. Not shown. Space separated words people might type. Translate as synonyms, not as a sentence.
keywords.settings: Hidden search keywords for settings entries in quick search. Not shown. Space separated words people might type. Translate as synonyms.
keywords.updates: Hidden search keywords for the check for updates action in quick search. Not shown. Space separated words people might type. Translate as synonyms.
keywords.support: Hidden search keywords for the support action in quick search. Not shown. Space separated words. Ko fi is a donation service name and stays as is.
keywords.palette: Hidden search keywords for the quick search shortcut entry. Not shown. Space separated words people might type. Translate as synonyms.
keywords.jump: Hidden search keywords for the jump to a page shortcut entry. Not shown. Space separated words people might type. Translate as synonyms.

crash.heading_unclean: Heading of the crash dialog shown on launch after the app closed unexpectedly. Contains "Deadlock+", which stays untranslated.
crash.heading_error: Heading of the crash dialog shown on launch after the app hit an error. Contains "Deadlock+", which stays untranslated.
crash.detail_unclean: Body text in the crash dialog under the heading, for an unexpected close. "It" is the app.
crash.detail_error: Body text in the crash dialog under the heading, for an error. A crash report file was written to the user's PC.
crash.attach_note: Body text in the crash dialog telling the user to attach the report file to a bug report. {file} = file name, e.g. "crash.txt". {path} = full folder path on the PC.
crash.meta: Small info line in the crash dialog. {time} = date and time of the crash. {version} = app version, e.g. "0.15.0". {os} = operating system, e.g. "Windows 11". "Deadlock+" stays untranslated.
crash.privacy: Small privacy note at the bottom of the crash dialog. "Settings" refers to the Settings page, match its translation.
crash.dismiss: Button in the crash dialog that closes it. Keep short, about 8 characters.
crash.open_folder: Button in the crash dialog that opens the folder holding the crash report. Keep short, about 20 characters.
crash.report_github: Primary button in the crash dialog that opens a new bug report on GitHub. GitHub stays untranslated. Keep short, about 18 characters.
crash.reveal_failed: Error message. Shown in the crash dialog when the folder with the crash report could not be opened in the file manager.
crash.issue_failed: Error message. Shown in the crash dialog when the browser page to file a GitHub issue could not be opened. GitHub stays untranslated.
crash.dismiss_failed: Error message. Shown in the crash dialog when closing or dismissing the crash report failed.

notification_list.title: Tooltip and screen reader label of the bell button that opens the notifications menu in the app header.
notification_list.unread_count: Screen reader label of the notifications bell when some are unread. {count} = number of unread notifications, e.g. 3. Plural forms.
notification_list.unread: Screen reader only text before an unread notification in the list, marked by a red dot. Not visible. Ends with a colon.
notification_list.mark_all_read: Small button at the top of the notifications menu that marks every notification as read. Keep short, about 14 characters.
notification_list.mark_read: Tooltip and screen reader label of a button on one notification that marks it as read.
notification_list.empty: Empty state in the notifications menu when there are no notifications.

relative.now: Relative time on a notification, for less than a minute ago. Keep short, about 8 characters.
relative.minutes: Relative time on a notification. {count} = minutes ago, e.g. 5. Keep short, about 8 characters.
relative.hours: Relative time on a notification. {count} = hours ago, e.g. 3. Keep short, about 8 characters.
relative.yesterday: Relative time on a notification for one day ago. Keep short, about 9 characters.
relative.days: Relative time on a notification. {count} = days ago, e.g. 4, always 2 or more. Keep short, about 8 characters.

error_page.title: Heading of the error screen shown in place of a page that crashed.
error_page.body: Body text on the error screen under the heading. Says the rest of the app still works.
error_page.retry: Button on the error screen that reloads the failed page. Keep short, about 10 characters.
error_page.copy: Button on the error screen that copies the error details to the clipboard. Keep short, about 14 characters.
error_page.open_logs: Button on the error screen that opens the logs in Settings > Diagnostics. Keep short, about 12 characters.
error_page.copied: Toast shown after the error details were copied to the clipboard.
error_page.copy_failed: Error toast shown when copying the error details to the clipboard failed.
error_page.unknown: Fallback error message used in the error details when the error has no message.

telemetry.notice: Toast shown once on first launch about anonymous usage data and error reports. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated. "Settings" refers to the Settings page.
telemetry.notice_action: Action button on the telemetry toast. Opens Settings > Privacy. Keep short, about 14 characters.

support.nudge: Toast shown once after a number of launches asking for support. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated.
support.action: Button (with a donation icon) that opens the support page, and the action button on the support toast. Contains "Deadlock+", which stays untranslated. Keep short, about 18 characters.

connectivity.offline: Banner at the top of the app shown when the PC has no internet connection. "Deadlock" is the game and stays untranslated.

whats_new.title: Page heading of the What's new page (release notes).
whats_new.subtitle: Subtitle under the heading of the What's new page. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated.
whats_new.empty: Empty state on the What's new page when there are no release notes.
whats_new.show_all: Button at the bottom of the What's new page that shows older releases too. Keep short, about 20 characters.
whats_new.back_home: Button at the end of the What's new page that goes back to the Home page. Keep short, about 14 characters.
whats_new.version: Release heading on the What's new page, e.g. "Version 0.15.0". Shown over older releases and read out by screen readers over the newest.
whats_new.count_added: Count of new additions in a release, in a row of totals on the What's new page. Plural. {count} = number of bullets, e.g. 83.
whats_new.count_changed: Count of changes in a release, in a row of totals on the What's new page. Plural. {count} = number of bullets, e.g. 13.
whats_new.count_fixed: Count of bug fixes in a release, in a row of totals on the What's new page. Plural. {count} = number of bullets, e.g. 24.
whats_new.index: Heading of the list of sections that jumps to each part of a release on the What's new page; screen readers also read it as the list's name. Keep short.
whats_new.section_general: Section heading for a release's smaller new additions, as in the game's own patch notes. Keep short.
whats_new.section_changes: Section heading for a release's changes, as in the game's own patch notes. Keep short.
whats_new.section_fixes: Section heading for a release's bug fixes, as in the game's own patch notes. Keep short.
whats_new.section_removed: Section heading for things removed in a release, as in the game's own patch notes. Keep short.

account.default_name: Fallback name of the user's Steam account in the sidebar account chip, used when no profile name is known.
account.none: Text in the sidebar account chip when no Steam account was found. Keep short, about 16 characters.
account.none_found: Tooltip on the sidebar account chip when no Steam account was found.
account.tooltip: Tooltip on the sidebar account chip. {name} = Steam profile name, e.g. "Sammi". {id} = numeric Steam account ID, e.g. 123456789.

jobs.run_failed: Error message. Shown when a background task (such as a scan or sync) could not be started.

addon_scan.title: Title of a background job in the jobs list. The job scans installed Deadlock mods. Keep short, about 15 characters.
addon_scan.description: Description of the mod scan background job. Shown under its title. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated. Frametimes means time per frame in the game.

patch_notes_index.title: Title of a background job in the jobs list. It prepares patch notes for search. Keep short, about 28 characters.
patch_notes_index.description: Description of the patch note search background job. Shown under its title.

server_block_sync.title: Title of a background job in the jobs list. It updates blocked server regions. Keep short, about 22 characters.
server_block_sync.description: Description of the server block update background job. Shown under its title. "Valve" and "Deadlock+" stay untranslated. Firewall rules are Windows firewall rules.

match_grades.title: Title of a background job in the jobs list. It updates the grades of recent matches. Keep short, about 22 characters.
match_grades.description: Description of the match grades background job. Shown under its title. Grades are letter ratings given to players.

policy.always: Option in a dropdown choosing what a background job does while Deadlock runs. This one lets it keep running at full speed. Deadlock is the game. Keep short, about 14 characters.
policy.pause_in_game: Option in a dropdown choosing what a background job does while Deadlock runs. This one pauses it. Deadlock is the game. Keep short, about 8 characters.
policy.slow_in_game: Option in a dropdown choosing what a background job does while Deadlock runs. This one runs it slower. Deadlock is the game. Keep short, about 12 characters.

status.paused: Status line for a background job that is paused. {title} = job title, e.g. "Scanning mods". "Deadlock" is the game and stays untranslated.
status.starting: Status line for a background job that just started, no progress yet. {title} = job title, e.g. "Scanning mods". Keep the three dots.
status.progress: Status line for a running background job. {title} = job title, e.g. "Scanning mods". {done} = items finished, e.g. 12. {total} = items in all, e.g. 40.
status.progress_labeled: Status line for a running job with a detail. {title} = job title. {done} = items finished, e.g. 12. {total} = items in all, e.g. 40. {label} = current item name, e.g. a file name.

status.off: Status text on a setting for submitting missing matches to the Deadlock API. Means the feature is switched off. Keep short, about 5 characters.
status.looking_for_login: Status line for the match submission feature. It is looking for a saved Steam login on this PC. Steam is the game platform.
status.last_pass_failed: Status line for the match submission feature when its last check failed. {error} = reason text, e.g. "No connection to Steam".
status.accounts: Plural part of a status line. {count} = number of Steam accounts used, e.g. 2. Inserted into the "Using ..." sentence.
status.using: Status line for the match submission feature. {accounts} = phrase like "2 Steam accounts". {delivered} = number of matches sent this session, e.g. 5.

own.reading_history: Status line while Deadlock+ reads the user's own match history to find matches the Deadlock API lacks. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated if present.
own.progress: Progress line while submitting missing matches. {delivered} = matches sent so far, e.g. 3. {missing} = total missing matches, e.g. 12. Each takes about 20 seconds.
own.matches: Plural phrase for a number of matches, inserted into other status sentences. {count} = number of matches, e.g. 5.
own.nothing_missing: Final status line when the run finished and no match was missing. The Deadlock API is a service with match data and stays a name.
own.done: Final status line when a run finished. {matches} = phrase like "5 matches" (from the plural phrase).
own.incomplete: Final status line when a run ended with some matches not recovered. {matches} = phrase like "5 matches". {failed} = number of failed matches, e.g. 2.
own.rate_limited: Final status line when Steam's daily limit stopped the run. {matches} = phrase like "5 matches" sent. Steam is the game platform.
own.stopped: Final status line when a run was stopped. {matches} = phrase like "5 matches" sent before stopping.
own.paused: Status line for a paused run. {left} = matches still to send, e.g. 7. Keep short, about 20 characters.
own.waiting_game: Status line for a run waiting for the game to close. {left} = matches still to send, e.g. 7. Deadlock is the game and stays untranslated.
own.waiting_limit: Status line when Steam's daily limit is reached. {continues} = phrase like "Continues at 6:30 PM" (from the continues sentences). Ends with a period.
own.continues_at: Phrase telling when a waiting run continues, same day. {time} = clock time, e.g. "6:30 PM". Inserted into the daily limit sentence.
own.continues_tomorrow: Phrase telling when a waiting run continues, next day. {time} = clock time, e.g. "6:30 PM". Inserted into the daily limit sentence.
own.continues_after_game: Short status for a match that waits to be submitted until the game closes. Shown in the missing match panel and a status line. Deadlock is the game, untranslated.
own.last_run: Status line about the previous submission run. {when} = time ago phrase, e.g. "2 hours ago". {delivered} = matches sent, e.g. 5. {left} = matches left, e.g. 3.
own.last_run_nothing_left: Status line about the previous submission run that finished everything. {when} = time ago phrase, e.g. "2 hours ago". {delivered} = matches sent, e.g. 5.
own.last_run_limit: Status line about the previous run that hit Steam's daily limit. {when} = time ago phrase, e.g. "yesterday". {delivered} = matches sent, e.g. 5. {left} = matches left, e.g. 3.
own.last_run_failed: Status line about the previous submission run that failed. {when} = time ago phrase, e.g. "2 hours ago".

ago.now: Time ago phrase for less than a minute, used inside the last run sentences. Lowercase.
ago.minutes: Time ago phrase used inside the last run sentences. {count} = minutes, e.g. 5. Plural forms. Lowercase.
ago.hours: Time ago phrase used inside the last run sentences. {count} = hours, e.g. 3. Plural forms. Lowercase.
ago.yesterday: Time ago phrase for one day ago, used inside the last run sentences. Lowercase.
ago.days: Time ago phrase used inside the last run sentences. {count} = days, e.g. 4. Plural forms. Lowercase.

about.version: Row label in the About card on Settings for the app version. Keep short, about 8 characters.
about.dev_build: Value in the About card for the app version of a development build. {version} = app version, e.g. "0.15.0".
about.running_as: Row label in the About card for the Windows account type the app runs under. Value is Administrator or Standard user. Keep short, about 12 characters.
about.system: Row label in the About card for operating system and CPU type. Keep short, about 8 characters.
about.data_folder: Row label in the About card for the folder where Deadlock+ stores its data. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated. Keep short, about 12 characters.
about.game_build: Row label in the About card, Deadlock section, for the game's build number. Deadlock is the game. Keep short, about 12 characters.
about.game_built: Row label in the About card, Deadlock section, for the date the game build was made. Keep short, about 12 characters.
about.source_revision: Row label in the About card, Deadlock section, for the game's source code revision number. Keep short, about 16 characters.
about.install_folder: Row label in the About card, Deadlock section, for the folder where the game is installed. Keep short, about 14 characters.
about.administrator: Value in the About card for the Windows Administrator account. Keep short, about 14 characters.
about.standard_user: Value in the About card for a normal Windows account without administrator rights. Keep short, about 14 characters.
about.root: Value in the About card for the root user on Linux. Keep short, about 6 characters.
about.regular_user: Value in the About card for a normal Linux user without root rights. Keep short, about 14 characters.

support_report.title: Section heading of the support report card in Settings.
support_report.description: Description under the support report heading. Explains the report is built locally and nothing is sent automatically. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated.
support_report.included: Text in the support report card listing what the report contains. "Deadlock" is the game and stays untranslated. "Deadlock+" stays untranslated.
support_report.create: Button in the support report card that builds the report. Keep short, about 22 characters.
support_report.refresh: Button in the support report card, replaces the create button after a report exists. Builds it again. Keep short, about 14 characters.
support_report.creating: Button text in the support report card while the report is being built. Keep the three dots. Keep short, about 22 characters.
support_report.preview: Screen reader label of the text box showing the built support report.
support_report.copy: Button with a copy icon in the support report card that copies the report text. Keep short, about 6 characters.
support_report.copied: Toast shown after the support report was copied to the clipboard.
support_report.copy_failed: Error toast shown when copying the support report failed.
support_report.save: Button with a save icon in the support report card that saves the report to a file. Keep short, about 6 characters.
support_report.save_filter: File type name in the save file dialog for the support report, which is a .txt file. Keep short, about 6 characters.
support_report.saved: Toast shown after the support report was saved to a file.
support_report.save_failed: Error toast shown when saving the support report failed. The log is in Settings > Diagnostics.
support_report.build_failed: Error toast shown when building the support report failed. The log is in Settings > Diagnostics.

api_busy.waiting: Notice shown where data could not load because the Deadlock API (the data service) is overloaded. {seconds} = seconds until the next retry, e.g. 12. Keep "s" as the seconds unit.
api_busy.retrying: Notice shown where data could not load because the Deadlock API (the data service) is overloaded. The app is retrying right now.
api_busy.try_now: Button in the API busy notice. Skips the countdown and retries now. Keep short, about 7 characters.

region.error_title: Error title. Shown in place of one section of a page when that section fails to render. Followed by a Retry button.
region.error_body: Error detail. Shown under the section error title. Says the rest of Deadlock+ is not affected. Deadlock+ stays untranslated.
region.retry: Button on error messages. Tries the failed action or section again. Keep short, about 5 characters.
region.page_title: Error title. Shown when a whole page fails to render. Followed by a Retry button.

announcements.dismiss: Tooltip and screen reader label of the icon button that hides a notice from the Deadlock+ team. The notice stays hidden for good. Deadlock+ stays untranslated.
